learning_objective: 🎯 Unify electricity and magnetism by exploring how changing fields propagate through space as light, radio, and X-rays!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Maxwell discovered a missing piece in Ampere's Law: A changing electric field (like between the plates of a charging capacitor) acts exactly like a physical current. He called this the Displacement Current, proving that changing electric fields create magnetic fields.

EM waves are self-sustaining. A changing electric field creates a changing magnetic field, which creates an electric field, and so on. They oscillate perfectly perpendicular to each other and perpendicular to the direction of travel (transverse nature).

All EM waves travel at exactly the same speed in a vacuum: $3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$, which is the speed of light ($c = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_0 \epsilon_0}}$). The ratio of the electric field to the magnetic field amplitude is always equal to $c$ ($E_0/B_0 = c$).

EM waves come in different sizes, classified by wavelength and frequency. From longest wavelength (lowest energy) to shortest (highest energy): Radio waves, Microwaves, Infrared, Visible Light, Ultraviolet, X-rays, and Gamma rays.

EM waves don't just carry information; they carry energy and momentum. When sunlight hits you, it warms you up (energy) and actually exerts a microscopic physical push on you called radiation pressure (momentum)!

fun_activity.title: 📱 The Foil Faraday Cage
fun_activity.instructions: Wrap your smartphone completely in a thick layer of aluminum foil. Try calling it from another phone. The foil blocks the radio frequency EM waves from reaching the antenna, so the phone will lose all signal!

exam_tips: 📌 Memorize the order of the EM spectrum and at least one key use for each type (e.g., Infrared for night vision, UV for water purification).
📌 A very common 1-mark question: Write the equation relating the speed of an EM wave to the permeability and permittivity of free space ($c = 1/\sqrt{\mu_0\epsilon_0}$).
📌 The direction of propagation of an EM wave is given by the cross product of the electric and magnetic field vectors ($E \times B$).
quick_recap: ⭐ Maxwell's equations unified electricity and magnetism, proving light itself is an electromagnetic wave.
⭐ Electric and magnetic fields in an EM wave are always in phase with each other, peaking at the exact same time.
⭐ Accelerated or oscillating charges are the fundamental source of all electromagnetic waves.
